heterogeneity.finding: The gap is constant from 1993 to 2006: the social-origin x enrolment-year interactions in Table A3 range from 0.00 to -0.04 and are mostly insignificant.
The class gap is the same across most of the GPA range (Figure 4, Table A4); the interaction is significant only in the top three deciles.
The class gap is smallest among selective programmes requiring a high GPA to enter (arts, architecture, medicine) and highest among less selective programmes (humanities, natural science).
The gap in risk of dropout is evenly distributed across institutions, but somewhat higher at the University of Copenhagen.
